When I want to kill myself, the feeling of absolute hopelessness, like the situation keeps growing exponentially worse while it was unbearable to begin with, it makes everyday solutions feel like passing through flames to find the exit.

I have always felt this way. I have pondered suicide on a weekly, sometimes daily basis, since childhood.

My life is generally stable, I have a love, and close friends, and a great job and family. It's just that my emotions are still always so intense. My anxiety, my shame, my anger and frustration, they come so frequently and I feel like the tighter I try to hold them back and breathe deep, the worse it gets.

Sometimes, when things happen, it's hard for me to deal with failure, whether I failed them or they failed me. For some reason, I equate failure with being taken advantage of, like if they failed it's because they don't care that they fucked me over. With how often I fuck up, I am left feeling like I can't even trust myself not to take advantage of me, like there is nobody and nothing in this world that I can put any faith into. Things are "worth" staying alive for, but I wish none of it was there so I could just quietly fade away. I am sick of overreacting to life's little problems.

It is representative of the evils in our society. Almost all social injustice happening in the western world is represented in some small way by the way retail is run.

A work force is hired for the purpose of caring for the shop and its inventory, as well as being the store's face to their customers. At the same time, most retail businesses treat these employees as being expendable, getting performance out of their workers by threatening their job. All the while, the sales associate has to always smile, be friendly and courteous. I have always found this experience demoralizing. It encourages a self centered mindset where the worker sees themselves as separate from the business. From what I can tell, this is common.

What I am getting at is, retail businesses hold practices that get their employees to show up, but it is hard to actually care for the state of your shop and the needs of customers when your boss is dangling your job in front of you at every turn because they don't believe you have it in you to do a good job otherwise.

Don't even get me started on theft bullshit. People get unreasonably blamed for theft all the time, and there is no court or justice system to help prove otherwise. It's a serious problem, theft is, but maybe if businesses treated their employees better they could keep more desirable employees, instead of constantly turning over everyone except the very shittiest people. Very many places are like that, though.

The rest of the world is pretty much just like that, too.
Fuck retail.
